title: When the Trail Burns
premise: Isandro Zhou, a railroad engineer who has spent three years hiding in the rhythm of survey work after a bridge collapse killed his crew, is handed a dying prospector's map of closed mountain lines and a promise to deliver it somewhere safe. The map leads him and a ragtag expedition—his stubborn foreman, a disgraced cartographer, and the prospector's estranged daughter—into territory the railroad sealed off for reasons no one will admit. As monsoon season closes in, Isandro must decide whether loyalty to his new companions matters more than the truth about what the closed lines were built to bury, and whether he can finally stop measuring life in miles. In the end, he brings everyone home alive, testifies to what they found, and chooses to stay with the found family that refused to let him stay invisible.
about_author: Tamsin Kavanagh is a former field surveyor who spent six years mapping remote rail corridors across three continents before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about people who find themselves in the spaces between destinations.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Three years into self-imposed exile on survey crews, Isandro measures his life in chainage markers and avoids attachments. A routine inspection of a closed line brings him face to face with a prospector collapsed at the tunnel mouth. Emotional beat: the numbness of a man who has stopped counting time.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The prospector, Mateo Reyes, trades a weathered map of sealed mountain lines for a promise: take it where it needs to go before the monsoon. He dies by morning. Isandro, bound by a promise he didn't want, studies the map and recognizes terrain he helped close. Beat: guilt rekindled.

chapters.title: A Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Isandro assembles an expedition from whoever will say yes: foreman Odile Brant, disgraced cartographer Pell Wexler, and Mateo's estranged daughter Suri, who arrives demanding answers. Each has something to prove or hide. Beat: reluctant alliance formed over shared damage.

chapters.title: The Closed Gate
chapters.summary: Suri's POV. The team breaches the first sealed section of line. Suri resents leading strangers through her father's obsession, but the map's accuracy unsettles her—Mateo knew this country intimately. They find fresh boot prints where no one should walk. Beat: unease beneath adventure.

chapters.title: What the Railroad Buried
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Inside an abandoned maintenance depot, Pell decodes old correspondence: the line wasn't closed for landslides but for something found during construction. He keeps this from the group, fearing what truth costs. Beat: the first lie of loyalty versus truth.

chapters.title: River of Rust
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A flooded viaduct forces a dangerous crossing; Odile nearly drowns saving the equipment, and Isandro freezes—haunted by the bridge collapse. Suri covers for him without judgment. Beat: shame surfacing, first crack in his armor.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Kilometer 44
chapters.summary: Suri's POV. They shelter with an old track-walker who never left when the line closed. He recognizes Mateo's map and warns them: others have come looking, men who pay well and leave nothing. Beat: warmth of unexpected kindness shadowed by threat.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A private security detail led by the polished Mr. Vasseur intercepts them, offering money for the map. Isandro refuses, and realizes the expedition is now being followed. Beat: stakes sharpen from survival to pursuit.

chapters.title: Suri's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Suri's POV. Around a fire, Suri admits she spent years hating her father for choosing maps over her. Reading his margin notes, she finds messages meant for her all along. Beat: grief transmuting into love; belonging begins.

chapters.title: The Long Climb
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. The route turns vertical through switchbacks above cloud line. Pell confesses why he was disgraced—he falsified a chart that killed no one but ended careers—and Odile, unexpectedly, forgives him. Beat: honesty as load-bearing structure.

chapters.title: Vasseur's Offer
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Vasseur corners Isandro alone and reveals he knows about the bridge collapse—that Isandro signed the survey that failed. The offer becomes blackmail: the map for silence. Beat: Isandro's past weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Fracture Line
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile discovers Isandro's secret deal and confronts him before the crew. Trust fractures; Suri takes the map and considers going on alone. Beat: lowest point—the found family splinters exactly when unity matters most.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Weather signs say the monsoon makes landfall in four days; their exit window is closing fast. Isandro stops running from his guilt and tells the crew everything about the bridge collapse himself. Beat: truth chosen over safety, family tentatively re-knit.

chapters.title: Into the Sealed Tunnel
chapters.summary: Suri's POV. They enter the great bore the railroad dynamited shut, following Mateo's final annotations. Deep inside, lantern light reveals what was buried: not ore, but a mass grave from a construction disaster the company covered up. Beat: horror and terrible understanding.

chapters.title: Names in the Rock
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Among the grave goods are worker records—hundreds of names erased from company rolls, including men whose families still wait. Pell photographs everything. The map was Mateo's witness, carried for forty years. Beat: the promise reframed as testimony.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Portal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Exiting the tunnel, they're ambushed by Vasseur's men. Odile holds the pass while the others escape with the evidence; she's captured buying them hours. Beat: sacrifice as the truest expression of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Racing the storm down the mountain with Suri and Pell, Isandro uses every engineering trick he knows—rigging crossings, reading water—to outrun both pursuers and flood. Beat: mastery reclaimed; the engineer who froze now leads flawlessly.

chapters.title: Trade for Odile
chapters.summary: Suri's POV. Suri engineers a trade: a decoy copy of the map for Odile, exploiting Vasseur's greed and Pell's forged-chart skills. It works, barely, and Vasseur realizes too late he's been played. Beat: cunning triumph; the strays operate as one mind.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The monsoon hits as they reach the valley railhead. In chaos and rising water, Vasseur makes one last attempt to seize the originals—and drowns pursuing them, undone by the same river the company ignored. Beat: nature settles accounts.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Safe in the city, the crew delivers the records to journalists and regulators. Isandro gives a full statement, including his own failures, refusing anonymity. The cover-up breaks open publicly. Beat: truth honored at last, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: Homecoming on the Open Line
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Weeks later, the reopened memorial train runs the old line with families of the lost aboard. Odile, offered her own crew, asks instead to keep this one together. Beat: belonging made official; grief given a place to rest.

chapters.title: Where the Trail Ends
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro declines a promotion that would scatter the team, choosing instead to lead surveys with the people who pulled him out of exile. Standing at the trailhead with Suri, he stops measuring miles and starts counting seasons—with them. Beat: quiet, earned resolution; the invisible man comes home.
